embeddingModels.name: Gemini Embedding 2
embeddingModels.description: Google's current embedding model (May 2026), 3072 dimensions, 8K context. Verified byte-identical between OpenRouter and Google's native API, on both bare and prefixed input -- OpenRouter passes it through faithfully. Note it dropped task_type: its semantic-similarity mode lives in a text prefix, not in input_type, which it ignores.
embeddingModels.inputTypeNote: Ignores input_type: its semantic_similarity output is byte-identical to sending nothing. The mode is delivered as a TEXT PREFIX on the document instead (task: sentence similarity | query: ...), which moves the vector to cosine 0.811 from bare text -- a far larger change than any parameter produces. Verified byte-identical between OpenRouter and Google native on both bare and prefixed input.

embeddingModels.name: Gemini Embedding 001
embeddingModels.description: Previous-generation Google embedding model, 3072 dimensions. Its DEFAULT output space is RETRIEVAL_QUERY: sending search_query returns the byte-identical vector to sending nothing, while semantic_similarity (cosine 0.860 from default) and search_document (0.910) are each a genuinely different space. That identity reads as "the default is this mode" rather than "the field was ignored", because on the very same call the other two values do move the vector -- so the field is provably being read. A library embedded with no mode is therefore in the QUERY space, which is the one tuned for encoding short searches rather than comparing whole documents.
embeddingModels.inputTypeNote: Setting a mode here REQUIRES pinning an upstream. OpenRouter serves this model from two that disagree: pinned to google-vertex, input_type: semantic_similarity is honoured and stable (cosine 0.841 from unmoded); pinned to google-ai-studio it is dropped and the unmoded vector comes back. Unpinned, each request is a coin flip and the library becomes a mixture of two spaces -- so the settings page refuses that combination. Both upstreams do agree on the unmoded vector, which is why the library embedded without a mode is unaffected however it routed.

embeddingModels.name: Qwen3 Embedding 8B
embeddingModels.description: Open-weights embedder, 4096 dimensions, 32K context. Instruction-aware, but its documented recipe puts the instruction on the QUERY side against bare documents -- there is no official symmetric recipe, so it does not take a retrieval mode here. OpenRouter routes it across several upstream providers unless routing is pinned.
embeddingModels.inputTypeNote: Takes no mode. Qwen is instruction-aware, but its documented recipe puts the instruction on the QUERY against bare documents, and this recommender has no text query -- the query is a centroid of item vectors. Prefixing every document identically is not an official Qwen form.

embeddingModels.name: Perplexity Embed V1 4B
embeddingModels.description: Perplexity's 4B retrieval embedding model, 2560 dimensions, 32K context -- by far the longest context of anything here, though this app's canonical text never approaches it. OpenRouter serves it from Perplexity alone: one upstream endpoint, so there is no routing to pin. That endpoint is int8-quantised, and the model card says the vectors come back UNNORMALISED, so the per-item l2Normalize in buildWeightedAverageEmbedding and refreshCenteredEmbeddings is load-bearing here rather than the identity it is for Gemini at its native 3072.
embeddingModels.inputTypeNote: Takes no mode, by design rather than omission: the model card states it is deliberately not instruction-tuned, so text is embedded bare with no task prefix to choose or maintain -- which also means no mode can be invented for it later the way gemini-2's prefix was measured. Matryoshka-truncatable to 128, which this app does not offer: `dimensions` is not plumbed, and a truncated vector needs the renormalisation storeEmbeddings does not do.
